full_judgment: 4. Defendant Nos. 1, 2, 3, 4-14, 15-35, 36-45, 46, 50-54, 55 and 47-49 filed separate written statements and additional written statements. In their written statement defendant Nos. 1 and 2 stated, inter-alia, that the plaintiff purchased 'Ka' scheduled land at taka 2,000, per decimal but he mentioned taka 20,000 in the deeds. Thereafter, the plaintiff transferred 'Ka' schedule land to different persons. The plaintiff did not spend taka 3,33,805.58 towards the development of the cattle market and the Government did not acknowledge the said amount. 'Ka' schedule land is the khas land of the Government and therefore, the plaintiff was not entitled to any compensation or value of the same.
